depth_findings.text: Manifest signing needs chain.KeyRing.SignPayload/VerifyPayload (chain/sign.go, not owned here); until the lead adds them the production manifest is unsigned, so the plan's 'manifest signature verifies with /keys' only holds in tests with a fake signer.

Deploy ordering and grant: nothing grants audit:compliance:read:self yet (compose and run-control-plane.sh are shared files), so the API is unreachable until the lead edits the credential block, and the audit-core image must be live before that block ships.

cmd/audit-verify cannot verify a sub-range export: it treats manifest last_seq as the head and reports truncated_below_attestation when the range stops before the newest attestation; it needs a range mode and it does not check the manifest signature yet.

Every compliance read appends a self-audit row to the org's chain (head lock, one more row per page), so heavy paging grows the chain and lengthens the head lock of a busy org; consider batching or a separate sink if export volume is high.
Denied attempts (member or viewer 403) are not self-audited; a denied-access row would help detection but opens a write-amplification path for any gateway user.

The six store tests that exercise the new SQL (range resolution by ingested_at, keyset paging, manifest ends, key listing) have not been executed: they skip without TEST_DATABASE_URL and docker is not allowed here.
Range resolution by ingested_at uses MIN/MAX(chain_seq) over audit_events filtered by ingested_at; on very large orgs this depends on idx_audit_events_org_ingested and has not been EXPLAINed.
/keys lists only the active key and the keys of the newest checkpoint and attestation because KeyRing cannot enumerate retired keys; a KeyRing.KeyIDs() would let it list the whole ring.

ValidateRequiredServiceCredentialRegistry does not require the compliance scope on the gateway (no API flag by design); if the owner wants a boot failure when the scope is missing it must be added there.

internal/store/store.go is outside the slice's owned file list and gains one field (manifestSigner PayloadSigner) plus its comment; it is only 2 added lines, needed for the signer seam, and the diff is otherwise clean, but the lead should explicitly accept it as a shared edit.

Needed before switching on: add KeyRing.SignPayload(payload) and VerifyPayload(keyID, payload, sig) in internal/chain/sign.go (nil-safe through CanSign, so a typed-nil ring yields ErrNoSigningKey and an unsigned manifest) and add the compliance scope to the gateway credential block; otherwise the API is unreachable and unsigned.

cmd/audit-verify treats manifest last_seq as the head and does not verify the manifest signature or support a sub-range export, so only a full-range export currently verifies offline; add a range mode before relying on sub-range exports as evidence.

The SQL in internal/store/compliance.go (MIN/MAX(chain_seq) by ingested_at range resolution, keyset paging with chain_seq > $2, thinning filters with ($n = '' OR col = $n), manifest ends, key listing) is unexecuted; it mirrors the verify.go query pattern (chainRowColumns + scanChainRow) and reads correctly, but must be proven on the DB harness before enabling.

Every compliance read appends a self-audit row to the org's chain (per-org head lock, one row per page), so heavy export paging grows the chain and lengthens head-lock contention for a busy org; fail-closed 500 on audit-write failure is correct but means a chain/DB outage also blocks reads.
Denied attempts (member or viewer 403) write no self-audit row; deliberately avoided to prevent write amplification by any gateway user, but a rate-limited denial audit would help detection.

Range resolution by ingested_at relies on idx_audit_events_org_ingested and has not been EXPLAINed on a large org; ingested_at is not commit-ordered so MIN/MAX over the window is a superset range, which is the intended contiguity trade-off.
/keys lists only the active key and the keys of the org's newest checkpoint and attestation because KeyRing has no enumeration; a KeyRing.KeyIDs() would let it list retired keys of older anchors.
ValidateRequiredServiceCredentialRegistry does not require the compliance scope on the gateway (no API flag by design); add it there only if the owner wants a boot failure when the scope is missing.

results.notes: Built the compliance read API under /v1/compliance/audit: GET /events, GET /manifest, POST /verify, GET /keys, GET /export-status (empty, exporter_enabled=false). New scope audit:compliance:read:self is accepted by the registry parser only for principal verevon-gateway; requiredAuditScope maps the five routes to it (a gateway with only audit:read:self gets 403, and the compliance scope does not unlock GET /v1/audit). requireComplianceRole(w, r) in roles.go returns the authorization only for owner/admin from the signed delegation, else 403 compliance_role_required; it is generic so F-t1-031 can import it. Events: limit default 200, cap 1000, opaque keyset cursor on chain_seq bound to the org, strict query allow-list, strict RFC3339 since/until that resolve to one contiguous chain_seq range (so an unfiltered range verifies offline), envelope {data, meta:{count,next_cursor,limit,head_seq}, error:null}; rows carry every preimage field plus prev_hash/row_hash/chain_version in the shape cmd/audit-verify reads. Every read writes a self-audit row (compliance_audit_read or compliance_audit_verify, plane control, producer audit-core) through InsertAuditFromSource and FAILS CLOSED: if the row cannot be written the response is 500 and no data is returned. Manifest JSON is a superset of the audit-verify manifest (org_id, last_seq, last_row_hash, checkpoint, attestation, legacy_unchained_rows plus first_seq, count, first_prev_hash, head_seq/head_hash, key_id, signature). Status is partial ONLY because the manifest signature cannot be produced by the production key ring yet: chain.KeyRing has no generic sign method and chain/ is not owned by this slice. The code signs through a store.PayloadSigner seam (payload ManifestPayload, magic VAM1, in store/compliance.go) and serves the manifest unsigned (still carrying the signed checkpoint and attestation) until the lead adds the two methods below. Also: KeyRing exposes no key listing, so /keys lists the active key plus the keys that signed the org's newest checkpoint and attestation (status active/retired/unavailable, public key base64url like AUDIT_CHAIN_PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64), which is what offline verification needs.
